summary:
GHOSTS OF SPACE — The Machines We Left Behind

GHOSTS OF SPACE is an interactive, animated educational documentary series that brings the stories of forgotten human-made machines left on the Moon, Mars, and other parts of space to life.The project aims to make space exploration interesting and easy to understand, especially for students. Through colourful 3D cartoon storytelling, viewers meet ORBIT, a friendly robot guide who takes them on journeys through real historical space missions, including Mars 3, Sojourner, Opportunity, and Cassini-Huygens.Unlike traditional documentaries, GHOSTS OF SPACE allows viewers to participate in the stories through interactive decisions and branching storylines. They can choose what a rover investigates, explore different scientific possibilities, and learn about the discoveries, challenges, and technology behind each mission.
The project uses publicly available NASA images, videos, scientific datasets, and mission information to ensure that the educational content is based on real space exploration.Technologies such as HTML, CSS, and JavaScript bring the interactive website, animations, and decision-based experiences together.Our goal is to turn forgotten space missions into exciting learning experiences, inspire curiosity about science and technology, and show how even machines that have stopped working can leave behind discoveries that change our understanding of the universe.
Their missions ended.Our curiosity never will.
details:
1. Project Title

GHOSTS OF SPACE: The Machines We Left Behind

2. Team Name

Zero Gravity X

3. Team Members

  • Anakha A
  • Geethika Vinod
  • Christine Julia Danie
  • Nora Susan Mathew
  • Aleena Binoy

4. Challenge Selected

Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars.

5. Project Type

Interactive educational website and animated documentary series.

6. Project Description

GHOSTS OF SPACE is an interactive storytelling platform that explores human-made machines left behind after space missions. It presents their journeys, discoveries, scientific importance, and mission endings through animated episodes and interactive choices.

7. Main Features

  • Interactive Homepage: A space-themed homepage introducing the project.
  • ORBIT: A friendly robot character who guides viewers through the series.
  • Animated Episodes: Cartoon documentaries based on real space missions.
  • Branching Storylines: Viewers make decisions that lead to different exploration paths.
  • Educational Content: Simple explanations of space science, robotics, and planetary exploration.
  • Historical Reconstructions: Visual recreations of important mission events, clearly distinguished from real footage.

8. Featured Space Missions

  1. Mars 3: The Soviet lander that transmitted from Mars for approximately 14.5 seconds.
  2. Moon Exploration Machines: Human-made equipment and robotic missions left on the lunar surface.
  3. Sojourner: NASA's first successful Mars rover.
  4. Opportunity: The Mars rover that operated for almost 15 years.
  5. Cassini-Huygens: The mission that explored Saturn and its moons.

9. Technologies Used

  • HTML — Website structure.
  • CSS — Design, animations, and visual effects.
  • JavaScript — Interactive buttons and branching storylines.
  • AI-assisted creative tools — Character, scene, and animation creation.
  • Browser text-to-speech — Narration.
  • NASA public resources — Mission images, videos, and scientific information.

10. NASA and Open Data Resources

  • NASA Image and Video Library.
  • NASA Planetary Data System (PDS).
  • NASA mission archives and educational resources.
  • Publicly available images and scientific mission records from other space agencies where relevant.

11. Target Audience

School students, young learners, space enthusiasts, and anyone interested in astronomy and robotics.

12. Main Objective

To make space exploration easier to understand through interactive storytelling while encouraging curiosity about science, technology, engineering, and the universe.

13. Expected Outcome

A user-friendly interactive website that transforms historical space missions into engaging educational experiences and helps students understand the importance of robotic space exploration.
